open_questions: Period confirmation after removing the two outlier ~3x deeper dips to see if a 10.0-d signal remains.
High-resolution spectroscopy to test for two stellar components at the 10 d orbital period implied by the primary/secondary alternation.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a ~514 ppm dip at 5.0 days that lands on the star, but odd and even dips differ by a factor of 3.6 (6 sigma) and the depth jumps from ~213 to 1763 to 31 ppm across sectors. That pattern and the two much deeper individual events are the signature of an eclipsing binary on the target folded at half its true ~10-day period, not a steady planet transit.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ at 6 sigma with a factor ~3.6 in depth, a classic sign of a binary at half the reported period (10.01 d). This strongly outweighs the small planet-like size (rp 1.8 Rearth) and on-target centroid.
Depth changes dramatically between sectors and even within SPOC 2-min (p 1.7e-16), inconsistent with a planet
True change within the same pipeline, not a calibration offset, correlated with the odd/even pattern (sector 29 = odd-like 1763 ppm)
Individual transits are completely inconsistent, dominated by two extreme events, ruling out a steady planet
Centroid pins the dip to the target, so the binary is on-target at 5.01 d = twice its true 10 d period
